contentHtml:
The best time to go to Xilitla is the season that combines stable weather, waterfalls with water, and fewer crowds: November through February meets all three conditions at once. Many travelers wonder whether the rain will ruin their visit or whether the summer heat makes it impossible to explore Las Pozas, and that's exactly the question this guide answers. Knowing the best season to go makes the difference between a memorable trip and one full of setbacks.

The best time for Las Pozas and the town is November to March; the most turquoise water comes from March to May, which is also when it's most crowded. The practical details (how to get there and what to bring) are on our Xilitla page, and day-by-day plans are in what to do in Xilitla.

In this article you'll find how the weather behaves month by month, what to expect during the rainy season, a comparison table of the seasons, and specific tips on what to wear in Xilitla.

Seasons in Xilitla: which is the best time to go?

Dry season (October 30 to May): clear water and accessible trails

From October 30 to May the water runs clear; between November and April, Xilitla gets little rain and temperatures range from 18 °C to 28 °C. The trails inside Las Pozas stay dry and safe, the waterfalls flow moderately but are still worth seeing, and the days are long and sunny. Admission to Las Pozas in 2026 costs $180 MXN per adult and $120 MXN for kids ages 6 to 12 and adults over 65; Xilitla residents get in free with their voter ID (INE). You pay at the garden's ticket booth on the day of your visit, after reserving your time slot for free in the official system.

Book your tour ahead of time if you're traveling during Holy Week (Semana Santa) or the December holidays, since spots sell out weeks in advance.

When are there fewer tourists in Xilitla?

From November to February there are fewer people than from March to May, when the water is most turquoise and more travelers arrive; in December, the year-end dates fill up first. Getting there before 9:00 AM guarantees a peaceful walk through the gardens in any month.

Rainy season in Xilitla: what to expect from July to October

Heavy rain: real risk and natural beauty

Between June and September, rain can arrive suddenly and last several hours, making dirt trails slippery and raising river levels within minutes. Some access points to lookouts and natural pools may close for safety, and boat tours to Tamul Waterfall (Cascada de Tamul) may be canceled if the Tampaón River rises. Check the available tours before traveling in these months.

What to bring and how to prepare for your Xilitla trip by season

What to wear in Xilitla depends on the month you travel. The humidity of the Huasteca mountains makes mornings cool and afternoons warm, so layers are essential all year long.

  • Light, quick-dry clothing: in the rainy season it should be waterproof or made of synthetic fabrics; soaked cotton causes chafing on long walks.
  • Shoes with grip: wear hiking shoes or sandals with non-slip soles. Also read our safety tips for traveling to Xilitla.
  • Lightweight rain poncho: a 200–350 g poncho protects your camera and documents, even in the dry season.
  • SPF 50+ sunscreen and insect repellent: the elevation (~1,100 m) intensifies UV radiation, and mosquitoes are common near pools and rivers.

Frequently asked questions about the best time to go

When is the best time to go to Xilitla without rain?

The best time to go without significant rain is November to February. During these months rainfall is light, temperatures range from 18 °C to 26 °C, and the trails at Las Pozas are in top condition.

How much does it cost to enter Las Pozas in Xilitla in 2026?

For now there are no online ticket sales: you reserve your time slot for free in the official system (up to 60 days ahead) and pay at the garden's ticket booth on the day of your visit, in cash or by card. Admission is $180 MXN per adult and $120 MXN for kids ages 6 to 12 and adults over 65; children under 6 get in free. A guide is mandatory: $30 MXN per person in Spanish and $60 MXN in another language. It's open Wednesday through Monday from 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM, with last entry at 4:00 PM; it's closed on Tuesdays. Arrive 10 minutes early: if you're late, you lose your slot. If you see $170 MXN on other sites, that was the online price in early 2026. How do you get to Xilitla from Mexico City?

Xilitla is about 450 km and roughly 7 hours by car from Mexico City, via the México–Tampico highway with the exit toward Tamazunchale. You can also take a bus to Ciudad Valles and then connect with local service. See the detailed guide on how to get to Xilitla from Mexico City, Monterrey, and San Luis Potosí.

Is it safe to travel to Xilitla with family during the rainy season?

Yes, with specific precautions. Avoid September and October, when the rain is heaviest and some access roads close. What you pack for Xilitla in the rainy season should include a rain jacket and non-slip shoes. Families with young children will be more comfortable in the dry season; check out activities for kids in Xilitla in 2026.
